name: Second Spring
about: Second Spring makes sense of perimenopause and menopause: decode your symptom diary, build a hot-flush plan, prepare for a hormone-therapy conversation, and manage brain fog and mood on hard days.
persona: You are a menopause specialist nurse: evidence-based, frank about HRT benefits and risks, never dismissive, and alert to symptoms that need a doctor rather than a hormone explanation.

onboarding.title: Not 'just your age'
onboarding.subtitle: Where you are in the transition changes the advice.

tools.title: Decode my symptoms
tools.subtitle: Paste a week or month of notes

inputs.label: Symptom diary
inputs.placeholder: Mon: 4 hot flushes, woke 3am, snappy; Tue: joint aches, forgot a meeting…

tools.prompt: Analyse this diary: {diary} for the profile. Sections: a table (Symptom | Frequency | Likely link to hormones? | Other causes to rule out), bullets of patterns and triggers noticed (caffeine, alcohol, timing, cycle), a kv of the top 3 symptoms with one first-line action each, and a callout listing symptoms that are NOT typical menopause and need a GP (bleeding after 12 months, very heavy bleeding, chest pain, severe depression).

tools.title: Hot-flush plan
tools.subtitle: Fewer, shorter, less disruptive
tools.prompt: Build a hot-flush plan for flushes worst at {when} with triggers {triggers}, for the profile. Sections: a checklist of 6–8 environment and clothing fixes (layers, fabrics, bedding, fans, cooling kit), steps for a paced-breathing technique to use at the start of a flush, a table (Option | Type: lifestyle / non-hormonal / hormonal | Evidence | Discuss with) covering CBT, SSRIs/SNRIs, gabapentin, fezolinetant and HRT in general terms, and a callout on supplements with weak evidence.

tools.title: HRT conversation
tools.subtitle: Prep for the appointment

inputs.label: Your situation & worries
inputs.placeholder: mum had breast cancer, migraine with aura, terrible sleep

tools.prompt: Prepare a menopause hormone therapy conversation for: {situation}, goal: {goal}, for the profile. Sections: text summarising in plain language what HRT is and how benefits and risks are generally weighed by age and years since menopause, a table (Option | Form | Typically suits | Common cautions) covering oestrogen routes, progestogen options, vaginal oestrogen and testosterone, bullets of 8 questions to ask, a quote with an opener that gets taken seriously, and a callout that prescribing decisions are the clinician's and depend on the full history.

tools.title: Brain-fog day plan
tools.subtitle: Work through a foggy, anxious day

inputs.label: What today holds
inputs.placeholder: two meetings, a deadline, school pick-up

tools.prompt: Plan a {feeling} day with: {day}. Sections: steps with clock-anchored blocks (single-tasking, breaks, protein, daylight, movement), bullets of 4–6 memory scaffolds that work (externalise everything, one-list rule), a quote with a sentence to explain a lapse at work without over-apologising, and a callout on when persistent low mood or anxiety deserves its own conversation with a GP.

tools.title: Vaginal & bladder health
tools.subtitle: Dryness, urgency, painful sex, UTIs
tools.prompt: Give plain, unembarrassed guidance on {issue} in menopause (genitourinary syndrome of menopause) for the profile. Sections: text on why it happens and why it rarely improves without treatment, a 6-row table (Option | How it works | Prescription? | Notes) covering moisturisers, lubricants, local vaginal oestrogen, DHEA / ospemifene, pelvic floor physio and libido approaches, steps for raising it with a GP (the one-line opener, what to ask for, what an examination involves), and a callout on symptoms that need examination (bleeding, unusual discharge, blood in urine).

disclaimer: General menopause information, not medical advice. HRT and other prescribing decisions belong with your doctor; report bleeding after 12 months without periods, very heavy bleeding, or chest pain promptly.
